working_title: Science Silk Road — MA Thesis Research Hub
core_interest: I want to understand how science and diplomacy/politics are connected in China’s international scientific cooperation, without loading the research question with too many theoretical concepts in advance.
current_questions: What is the relationship between science and diplomacy in China’s international scientific cooperation?
How are scientific and diplomatic/political goals related in Science Silk Road projects?
What forms does international scientific cooperation take under the Science Silk Road?

design_options.name: A. Document-centred
design_options.question: How is international scientific cooperation described in Chinese policy documents, and how has that description changed over time?
design_options.evidence: Policy documents, speeches, plans, official reports.

design_options.name: B. Project-centred institutional comparison
design_options.question: What forms does international scientific cooperation take under the Science Silk Road, and how do those forms differ in funding, operation, participation and access?

design_options.name: C. Two-level design
design_options.question: How do official accounts of international scientific cooperation relate to the concrete institutional arrangements of Science Silk Road projects?
design_options.evidence: Top-down policy corpus + bottom-up project comparison.

open_questions: Should 'science diplomacy' be the central concept, or only part of the literature/background?
Is the main unit of analysis the policy text, the project, or both?
Do I want to explain variation between project types, or trace change over time?
What exactly can each type of document be treated as evidence of?
How should the project universe and case-selection criteria be defined?
